title: The Last Salt
premise: Emrys Winterbourne, a nonbinary runaway apprentice and smuggler's guide, learns that a century-old prophecy book names them as the 'last salt'—the final heir of Thornfell, a drowned kingdom erased from maps and law. Hunted by the Crown's Inquisitors and the prophecy's original authors alike, Emrys must gather the scattered relics of Thornfell's inheritance and find the Door, the only passage into the country that exists now only in memory. The thirteenth moon brings a choice: restore Thornfell and inherit its corrupting crown of power, or unmake it forever, taking justice into their own hands outside any law. Emrys chooses to dissolve the kingdom, freeing its ghost-people and burning the prophecy itself.
about_author: Rosalind Coldharbour is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires in a coastal customs house. They write fantasy about borders, bureaucracy, and the people who slip through both.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Almanac
chapters.summary: Emrys guides a contraband shipment through the Thornfell passes, showing their mastery of hidden roads and their hunger to stay unnamed. A client pays partly in an old book; that night Emrys finds tonight's date circled in its prophecies. POV: Emrys. Beat: unease—the invisible life begins cracking.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: Emrys brings the book to their estranged mentor, hedge-witch Maren, who recognizes the script as Royal Saltwork cipher and goes pale at Emrys's name written within. She urges flight; Emrys refuses to run blind. POV: Emrys. Beat: dread mixed with stubborn curiosity.

chapters.title: The Grey Inquisitor
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Halvard Vane arrives in the valley town, questioning innkeepers about a 'salt-marked child.' Emrys watches from a loft as Vane burns Maren's cottage for harboring prophecy. POV: alternating Emrys and Vane. Beat: grief hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Maps Forgot
chapters.summary: Fleeing north, Emrys follows the book's marginalia to a village that appears on no map—a place where Thornfell's ghosts still pay taxes to no one. An old ferryman explains the kingdom was dissolved by treaty, not conquest. POV: Emrys. Beat: wonder shadowed by injustice.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: The ferryman deciphers the prophecy's frame: on the thirteenth new moon, the Door opens once, and only the last salt may choose what passes through. Eleven turns remain. Vane's riders reach the river behind them. POV: Emrys. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: A Thief of Relics
chapters.summary: Emrys allies with Sable Quill, a charming relic-thief who has been selling 'Thornfell junk' for years without knowing its worth. Their first target: the Salt Crown's circlet hidden under a chapel floor. POV: Sable. Beat: wary partnership, first spark of trust.

chapters.title: The Chapel Heist
chapters.summary: The heist succeeds but triggers a ward that marks Emrys visibly with the salt-sigil—no longer invisible to magic or Inquisitors. Sable sees the mark and understands who they've been traveling with. POV: Emrys. Beat: exposure; identity can no longer be shed.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vane captures Sable and offers Emrys amnesty in exchange for the relics and renunciation of the inheritance. Emrys refuses, springing Sable from custody and learning Vane answers not to the Crown but to the prophecy's secret authors. POV: Vane. Beat: the true enemy revealed.

chapters.title: The Order of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapters via Vane's interrogation notes reveal the Ledger, a century-old order of clerks who wrote the prophecy to manufacture a lawful heir—and a lawful erasure—of Thornfell. POV: Vane. Beat: horror at how power writes its own justice.

chapters.title: Ghost Country
chapters.summary: Emrys and Sable cross into the heartland where the dead still farm phantom fields. Emrys meets the ghost of Queen Ilsa, last ruler of Thornfell, who confesses her own corruption and begs not to be restored. POV: Emrys. Beat: compassion complicating duty.

chapters.title: The Second Relic
chapters.summary: Retrieving the Salt Chalice from a drowned cathedral, Emrys nearly drowns and is saved by Sable, who confesses they were hired by the Ledger to track the last salt all along. POV: Sable. Beat: betrayal and forgiveness tangled together.

chapters.title: Maren's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Reunited briefly with the dying Maren, Emrys receives her final teaching: power isn't taken or given, it's agreed upon—and agreements can be refused. She dies holding the prophecy open to Emrys's page. POV: Emrys. Beat: mourning transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Summons
chapters.summary: The Ledger offers Emrys the crown outright: become Thornfell's restorer, their puppet king, and the border wars end. Emrys sees the trap—inherited power as gilded cage—and publicly refuses at a border town assembly. POV: Emrys. Beat: defiance before witnesses.

chapters.title: Turn Twelve
chapters.summary: With one turn left, Vane corners them in the high passes; Sable takes a crossbow bolt meant for Emrys. Emrys uses the circlet's power for the first time to drive Vane off—and feels how sweet it tastes. POV: Emrys. Beat: corruption's first taste, terrifyingly pleasant.

chapters.title: The Weight of Salt
chapters.summary: Wearing the circlet overnight, Emrys dreams Thornfell's history from the throne's view and wakes craving the chalice's completion. They confide in the recovering Sable, asking to be watched. POV: Emrys. Beat: self-knowledge as armor against the crown.

chapters.title: Where the Door Sleeps
chapters.summary: Guided by the ghost-ferryman, they reach the Door: a seam in a cliff face that opens only for the last salt on the thirteenth turn. The Ledger's full company and Vane arrive to besiege the valley. POV: alternating. Beat: the stage set for climax.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Seam
chapters.summary: The Ledger's clerks bind the ghosts as leverage; Vane, disgusted by his masters' cruelty, wavers. Emrys fights through using relic-power, each act of strength deepening the salt-corruption visible on their skin. POV: Emrys. Beat: victory and corrosion in the same breath.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Vane turns on the Ledger, revealing their founding crime: they poisoned Thornfell's wells a century ago to force its dissolution and profit from the treaty. He gives Emrys the evidence and stands aside. POV: Vane. Beat: redemption bought too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Under the dark moon, Emrys opens the Door. Inside waits Thornfell whole and living, and the crown offering itself. Queen Ilsa's ghost stands beside them, refusing again. POV: Emrys. Beat: stillness before the irrevocable.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: Emrys carries the relics through the Door and speaks refusal—not restoration but dissolution—returning the kingdom's power to its people, living and dead, and shattering the crown. The Door closes forever; the ghosts fade free. POV: Emrys. Beat: sacrifice as justice outside every law.

chapters.title: Ash and Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys burns the prophecy book before the assembled townsfolk, ending the inheritance of fate itself. The Ledger collapses as its crime becomes public; Vane accepts trial by no court but the people he wronged. POV: Vane. Beat: accountability without throne or gallows.

chapters.title: The Road Without a Name
chapters.summary: Seasons later, Emrys and Sable guide travelers through Thornfell's passes—now just mountains again, mapped by those who live there. Emrys keeps one grain of salt in a locket: memory, not crown. POV: Emrys. Beat: quiet freedom, chosen and ordinary.
